title: Acyclic resolutions
statement:
Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor between
abelian categories with enough injectives. If $F\to A^\bullet$ is a resolution
and each $A^m$ is $v$-acyclic, then

$$
\mathcal H^q(vA^\bullet)\simeq R^qvF.
$$

More generally, for a bounded below complex $A^\bullet$ of $v$-acyclic
objects, the canonical comparison $vA^\bullet\to Rv(A^\bullet)$ is an
isomorphism in $D^+(\mathcal B)$.

proof.text: For the resolution assertion, use its nonnegative augmented exact complex $0\to F\to A^0\to A^1\to\cdots$. Set $Z^0=F$ and $Z^{m+1}=\operatorname{im}(A^m\to A^{m+1})$ for $m\geq0$. Exactness identifies $Z^m$ with $\ker(A^m\to A^{m+1})$, giving short exact sequences $0\to Z^m\to A^m\to Z^{m+1}\to0$. Here cohomology means kernel modulo image, and $v$-acyclic means $R^av(A^m)=0$ for all $a>0$.

source.place: Tag 05TA (proposition-enough-acyclics), proof: break an exact complex into its image/cycle short exact sequences; blueprint imported proof paragraph 1.

proof.text: Apply the long exact derived sequence to each sequence in step 1. Identify $R^0v$ with $v$ using its natural degree-zero isomorphism. Since $R^av(A^m)=0$ for $a>0$, the segment $vA^m\to vZ^{m+1}\to R^1vZ^m\to0$ identifies $\operatorname{coker}(vA^m\to vZ^{m+1})$ with $R^1vZ^m$. For every $a\geq1$, the segment $0\to R^avZ^{m+1}\to R^{a+1}vZ^m\to0$ gives $R^avZ^{m+1}\simeq R^{a+1}vZ^m$.

source.place: Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), parts (1)–(2); Tag 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived), part (3); blueprint imported proof paragraph 1.

proof.text: Left exactness identifies $\ker(vA^q\to vA^{q+1})$ with $vZ^q$: factor the differential through $Z^{q+1}\hookrightarrow A^{q+1}$, whose image under $v$ is still monic, and use the kernel sequence of step 1. Thus for $q\geq1$, $\mathcal H^q(vA^\bullet)=\operatorname{coker}(vA^{q-1}\to vZ^q)\simeq R^1vZ^{q-1}\simeq R^2vZ^{q-2}\simeq\cdots\simeq R^qvZ^0=R^qvF$, by the successive isomorphisms of step 2. For $q=1$ there are no further shifts; for $q=0$ the kernel is $vZ^0=vF\simeq R^0vF$.

source.place: Tag 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived), part (3), and the cohomology definition; blueprint imported proof paragraph 2.

proof.text: Now let $A^\bullet$ be the bounded below complex in the second assertion and choose $a\in\mathbf Z$ with $A^n=0$ for $n<a$. The bounded below injective replacement theorem gives a quasi-isomorphism $s:A^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ with every $J^n$ injective and $J^n=0$ for $n<a$. Each $J^n$ is $v$-acyclic by injective vanishing. The zero object is injective because every map into it is the unique zero map and hence extends across every monomorphism; in particular zero is also $v$-acyclic.

Form the cochain mapping cone $C=\operatorname{Cone}(s)$ with $C^n=J^n\oplus A^{n+1}$ and differential $\begin{pmatrix}d_J^n&s^{n+1}\\0&-d_A^{n+1}\end{pmatrix}$. Since $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism, the cone criterion says $C$ is acyclic. The displayed terms vanish for $n<a-1$, so $C$ is bounded below with lower bound $b=a-1$.

source.place: Tag 05TA (proposition-enough-acyclics), proof, cone C(s); Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic) with the cone triangle and its cohomology sequence.

proof.text: Every term $C^n$ is $v$-acyclic. Indeed, apply the long exact derived sequence to the split short exact sequence $0\to J^n\to J^n\oplus A^{n+1}\to A^{n+1}\to0$. For each $r>0$ its exact segment $R^rvJ^n\to R^rvC^n\to R^rvA^{n+1}$ has both outside objects zero, by step 4 and the hypothesis on $A^\bullet$; therefore the middle object is zero. This establishes the needed closure under the binary direct sum without assuming that $v$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), part (1), applied to a split sequence; Tag 05TA, proof: the cone terms are acyclic.

proof.text: Put $T^n=\ker(C^n\to C^{n+1})$. Acyclicity gives short exact sequences $0\to T^n\to C^n\to T^{n+1}\to0$. For $n<b$ the cycles are zero, and $T^b=\operatorname{im}(C^{b-1}\to C^b)=0$. Induct on $n\geq b$, with inductive assertion that $R^rvT^n=0$ for every $r>0$. The base is zero acyclicity from step 4. For the induction step, the long exact sequence and step 6 give $R^rvT^{n+1}\simeq R^{r+1}vT^n=0$ for every $r>0$. The same sequence in degree zero, using $R^0v=v$ and $R^1vT^n=0$, gives $0\to vT^n\to vC^n\to vT^{n+1}\to0$. Since $v$ preserves kernels, $vT^n=\ker(vC^n\to vC^{n+1})$, and surjectivity of $vC^{n-1}\to vT^n$ shows that this kernel is exactly the image of $vC^{n-1}\to vC^n$. Hence $vC$ is acyclic in every degree, including degrees below $b$.

source.place: Tag 05TA (proposition-enough-acyclics), proof, induction on cycles of an exact bounded below complex; Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), parts (1)–(2).

proof.text: The canonical biproduct comparison $v(J^n\oplus A^{n+1})\simeq vJ^n\oplus vA^{n+1}$ identifies $vC$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(v(s))$ as complexes: additivity sends the differential matrix in step 5 to $\begin{pmatrix}v(d_J^n)&v(s^{n+1})\\0&-v(d_A^{n+1})\end{pmatrix}$, since it preserves sums, zero and negatives. Thus step 7 says that $\operatorname{Cone}(v(s))$ is acyclic. Applying the cone criterion in $\mathcal B$ shows $v(s):vA^\bullet\to vJ^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05TA (proposition-enough-acyclics), proof, reduction to the acyclic mapping cone; the additive functor preserves its defining differential matrix.

proof.text: Let $\alpha_L:Q_{\mathcal B}(vL)\to Rv(Q_{\mathcal A}L)$ be the canonical natural comparison for the bounded below right derived functor. Its existence and the fact that $\alpha_J$ is an isomorphism for the bounded below injective complex $J$ are precisely the bounded below injective computation theorem. Naturality at $s$ is $Rv(Q_{\mathcal A}s)\circ\alpha_A=\alpha_J\circ Q_{\mathcal B}(v(s))$. The factor $Q_{\mathcal B}(v(s))$ is invertible by step 8 and localization at quasi-isomorphisms; $Rv(Q_{\mathcal A}s)$ is invertible because $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $Rv$ is a functor. Therefore $\alpha_A=Rv(Q_{\mathcal A}s)^{-1}\circ\alpha_J\circ Q_{\mathcal B}(v(s))$ is an isomorphism in $D^+(\mathcal B)$. This proves the canonical comparison itself, and completes the second assertion.

tool_uses.why: The unit explicitly needs the long exact sequences for its cycle sequences; this general homological-algebra tool supplies them, without replacing dimension shifting.

The mapping-cone argument needs exactly the equivalence between quasi-isomorphisms and acyclic cones, in both abelian categories; this is a generic complex-theory tool.
